name: YPF Sociedad Anonima
moat_justification: YPF holds a real resource-cost advantage: it is the largest operator in Vaca Muerta (the world's second-largest unconventional gas reserve and fourth-largest shale-oil reserve) and dominates Argentine refining and fuel marketing. But it is a commodity price-taker whose durability is hostage to its controlling shareholder — the Argentine state (51%) — with the 2012 Repsol expropriation, a history of domestic fuel-price controls, and ARS/sovereign risk repeatedly overriding shareholder economics. Resource quality earns a weak-moat score, not a moderate one.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency ARS converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (YPF Form 20-F, Item 9 (Shares and ADSs) and the Amended and Restated Deposit Agreement dated March 9, 2022 filed with the 20-F: each ADS represents one Class D share) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -0.34 vs 3-yr median 0.60 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.2% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 30.8x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: State-controlled Argentine integrated oil major with a world-class Vaca Muerta resource but a weak, sovereign-capped moat (4/10) — on owner's earnings after full capex it clears nothing: weighted IRR 3.6%, weighted IV@15 $4.38 vs the $51.11 ADS price; the market is paying for shale growth and EBITDA that this screen charges as capex. Clears 15% only below ~$4.38.
moat_for: Largest Vaca Muerta operator — world-class shale resource (2nd-largest unconventional gas, 4th-largest shale oil globally) with falling shale unit costs
Dominant Argentine downstream position — refining and fuel-marketing leadership with integrated logistics
Scale and infrastructure incumbency in Argentine energy (pipelines, refineries, retail network) that rivals cannot replicate quickly
moat_against: Argentine state controls 51% — political override risk; 2012 Repsol expropriation precedent and a history of fuel-price controls
Pure commodity price-taker — earnings swing with Brent and ARS; no pricing power over its main product
Capital intensity consumes the cash engine — FY2025 capex of $5,077M vs OCF of $4,959M; growth must be bought with capex every year
Sovereign/FX exposure — ARS reporting currency, Argentine macro and capital-control cycles sit between operations and USD shareholders
